rule.description: A contiguous group of >= 3 adjacent scalar or slice-of-scalar parameters with at least one collection member, whose exact parameter type sequence recurs in >= 2 distinct function or method signatures across >= 2 distinct production files, is credited as a loose record bundle and every signature carrying it is reported; supporting evidence (unsplit forwarding between carriers, origin call sites handing the loose members to a carrier, and fragment signatures reusing an in-order subset of the bundle) is reported alongside the carriers.

checks.description: Detect signatures that declare a cohesive record's fields as individually typed parameters whose exact type group recurs across >= 2 signatures in >= 2 production files.
checks.detected_relation: function signature -> loose always-together record parameter group recurring across signatures and files
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The domain entry already exists as one record in the configuration model; re-declaring its field group in every signature is the data-clump relation and forces every consumer to repeat and re-thread the same values.

matches.evidence: Loop entry declares the domain as individually passed parameters [domainName string, subDomains []string, providerName string] after the loop context, and forwards them unsplit to Handler.UpdateIP.
One-shot update entry declares the same loose group [domainName string, subDomains []string, providerName string] and forwards it unsplit to Handler.updateDNS.

Record-update step declares [domainName string, subDomains []string, providerName string] plus the current IP, keeping the domain fields loose through the step that actually dispatches to the provider.

Startup per-domain validation helper receives the re-declared field group [domainName string, subDomains []string, providerName string] plus the config, validating a domain entry one loose field at a time.

checks.description: Detect signatures that reuse, in order, a subset of a credited bundle's member (name, type) pairs as adjacent parameters.
checks.detected_relation: helper signature -> in-order subset of a credited loose record bundle's member parameters
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: A helper picking up only some of the always-together fields shows the record has no single authoritative consumer boundary; the clump is spreading into partial signatures.

matches.evidence: Provider resolution declares [domainName string, providerName string], reusing the record's name+provider fields in order (skipping the subdomain list) of the credited bundle [string|[]string|string].

checks.description: Detect call sites that receive or construct >= 3 identifiers matching a credited bundle's member names and hand them, unsplit, to a carrier.
checks.detected_relation: caller -> unsplit handoff of a credited loose record bundle into a carrier signature
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The values only ever travel as the full group — origin and forwarding sites are the propagation paths that make the loose group a recurring contract rather than a local choice.

matches.evidence: The loop entry (after its own immediate run) passes domainName, subDomains, providerName unchanged to Handler.UpdateIP on every tick.
The one-shot entry passes domainName, subDomains, providerName (with the current IP appended) to Handler.updateDNS.
The manager's fan-out destructures each configured domain entry into domainName, subDomains, providerName locals and hands them to Handler.LoopUpdateIP for the background per-domain loop.
The manager's fan-out hands the same destructured field locals to Handler.UpdateIP on the synchronous RunOnce path.

excluded.reason: The provider backends' public three-string update contract (name, subdomain, IP) is a stable interface boundary with no collection member; folding the domain record into it would be an API redesign, so it is intentionally outside this rule's scope.

excluded.symbol: Domain record type and GetDomainProvider accessor
excluded.reason: This is the record abstraction itself — the intended post-repair shape, not a location where the domain travels as loose values.

excluded.symbol: test call sites of the update loop
excluded.reason: Mechanical compilation adaptation of test call sites; test files are outside the production analysis scope of the rule.
